questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language, the culture and the reputation of the hospital.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult in the beginning with the communication forward and backward between the two opportunities, but it all work out well at the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing i remember of

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got the email for the landlord im living with from some earlier students. Look for appartments at idealista (app or website) or ask in the whatsapp group with the other students (you can find it through the facebooksite for either Gijon or Oviedo).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitiely recomend to live in the area "l'arena" - it is close to the sea, a park and there are a lots of bars and restaurents. Most of the other students live there too.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I've been living in an appartment with three other people, and one was the landlord. I would recomend to live with your landlord, but it has been alright.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They are super nice and helpful when you arive but before the comunication is difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had practics at the departments: Pediatrics, gynecology, urgencias and anestesiology. I planned it with the secretary on e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I cant remember to be honest

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the four departments i asked for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont worry about the proces, it will be nice when you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They are extremely nice and patient at the hospital. If you want to learn and if you speak spanish you have a golden opportunity to learn a lot. Usually the spanish students hear dont do much practices (only the last year and they observe most of the time), so if you want to get hands on just ask the doctors or the nurses. They are super nice and will help you.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didnt have any classes. It is a small hospital, and they are usually not as busy as the doctors in Denmark, so they have more time to teach/discuss if you show interest.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Gynecology, pediatrics, urgencias and anestesiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially anestesiology because you can a lot of hands on work. In pediatrics the students usually have their first week in urgencias where you also can see a lot. Urgencias is interesting to see also, because there are a lot of patients and you can talk with the patients and do examinations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some, especially in Oviedo, but i didnt use it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
To go around in Asturias and hike. There are a lot of beautiful routes. And also a lot of beautiful places along the coast. 
Every friday there are a english pubquiz in Cimadevilla. 
You can easily buy a surfboard and sell it again (wallapop is a nice app for selling used stuff).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
To go around in Asturias and hike. There are a lot of beautiful routes. And also a lot of beautiful places along the coast. 
Every friday there are a english pubquiz in Cimadevilla. 
You can easily buy a surfboard and sell it again (wallapop is a nice app for selling used stuff).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, they are super friendly. The only thing is that they eat late and they have siestas, but for me it was easy to adjust to. They dont speak much english though, be prepared for that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the facebook and whatssapp groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language otherwise nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being very open, friendly, curious, welcoming and sweet.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have a good level of spanish, they dont eat much at the hospital (bring snacks og go to the cafeteria (it is cheap)), ask for doing things at the hospital.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first month before arriving the university offers language classes in spanish.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience the spanish peoples culture and also meet Erasmus students from all over the world with different cultures. To improve my spanish and to push my limits. Also here you experience another ambience at the hospital different from most danish hospitals. People here dont live for working but work for living.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and the communication with the universities before ariving.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are thinking about doing it, do it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
